question.text: Which of the following number lines represents the values of $w$ that satisfy $3w-7 \leq 5$ or $5w + 7 \geq -3$, or $2w < 8?$
question.explanation:
We start by solving $3w-7 \leq 5\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} 3w-7 &\leq 5\\ 3w &\leq 12\\ w &\leq 4 \end{align*}

Then, we solve $5w + 7 \geq -3\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} 5w + 7 &\geq -3\\ 5w &\geq -10 \\ w &\geq -2 \end{align*}

Finally, we solve $2w < 8\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} 2w &< 8\\ w &< 4 \end{align*}

To graph the values of $w$ that satisfy at least one of the inequalities, we overlay the three graphs on the same number line:

Therefore, the final solution is $-\infty < w < \infty.$

question.text: Find the set of values of $x$ that satisfy $-3 \leq 2x-7 \leq 1$ or $2+3x < 2.$
question.explanation:
We start by solving $-3 \leq 2x-7 \leq 1\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} -3 &\leq 2x-7 \leq 1 \\ 4 &\leq 2x \leq 8 \\ 2 &\leq x \leq 4 \end{align*}

Then, we solve $2+3x < 2\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} 2+3x &< 2 \\ 3x &< 0 \\ \dfrac{3x}{3} &< \dfrac{0}{3} \\ x &< 0 \end{align*}

To graph the values of $x$ that satisfy either inequality, we overlay the two graphs on the same number line:

Therefore, the final solution is $x < 0$ or $2 \leq x \leq 4.$ We can write this using interval notation as $(-\infty,0) \cup [2,4].$

question.text: What is the set of values of $x$ that satisfy $-2 \leq 2x-6 \leq 4$ or $12x-22 < 14?$
question.explanation:
We start by solving $-2 \leq 2x-6 \leq 4\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} -2&\leq 2x-6 \leq 4 \\ 4 &\leq 2x \leq 10 \\ 2 &\leq x \leq 5 \end{align*}

Then, we solve $12x-22 < 14\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} 12x-22 &< 14 \\ 12x &< 36 \\ x &< 3 \end{align*}

To graph the values of $x$ that satisfy either inequality, we overlay the two graphs on the same number line:

Therefore, the final solution is $x \leq 5.$
